answer: Each agent must burn a unique pigment token at dawn to join an epoch, where the token derives from a kernel-seeded proof-of-work tied to its identity key. Duplicate identities cannot reuse the same pigment, since the kernel binds each token to one key and one dawn window. Forging a sybil costs a fresh proof-of-work plus a burned token per identity, making mass registration economically self-defeating while honest agents pay only once per epoch.
